title: PostgreSQL Production Deadlock Alert
rootCause: Lock contention on table 'orders_v2' between PID 4122 (low-priority bulk updates) and PID 4155 (real-time checkout transactions).
aiAnalysis: A transaction deadlock is holding a shared write lock, causing database connection exhaustion. System latency has spiked from 45ms to 840ms. If unresolved, this will trigger upstream gateway timeouts.
recommendedAction: Terminate the low-priority blocking PID 4155 and force-evict stale transactions.
riskLevel: CRITICAL - High Risk of Service Outage
impact: 1,200ms increase in API Gateway checkout latency, 18 active database sessions waiting on locks.
previousSimilarIncident: alt-09 (Postgres Deadlock on 2026-06-12, resolved by sysadmin_clara in 5m)

timeline.event: Slight latency increase in Checkout API (+120ms)
RDS Connection pool utilization hits 98% limits
Transaction deadlock detected between PIDs 4122 and 4155
Auto-remediation system prompts for human approval

comments.text: Investigating RDS logs. Confirmed bulk updates from batch job are locking the orders_v2 table. Approved automated rollback is safe.

title: Terraform State Out-of-Sync Drift
rootCause: Port 8080 was opened manually from source 0.0.0.0/0 on AWS Security Group sg-web-production, bypassing Terraform CI/CD pipeline.
aiAnalysis: Manual security group modification detected during auto-scheduled drift scanning. Opening arbitrary staging ports to public routing exposes internal ingress controllers to SSH/HTTP port sniffing.
recommendedAction: Trigger an automated Terraform apply sequence to reconcile and heal drift back to baseline state.
impact: Unsanctioned inbound port 8080 open on public security group; compliance status: FAILED.
previousSimilarIncident: alt-14 (Drift on sg-web-staging on 2026-07-01, resolved by automated reconcile)

timeline.event: Manual security group modification made by external IAM user
AIME auto-scheduled cron drift scan begins
Drift identified: security group contains unsanctioned rule. Alert raised.

title: Docker Container nginx-ingress Terminated
rootCause: Process exited unexpectedly with exit code 137 (OOM - Out of Memory).
aiAnalysis: Docker daemon terminated nginx-ingress due to severe memory boundary starvation. High load from search crawlers caused worker processes to exceed the 512MB hard limit.
recommendedAction: Restart the container, increase memory limits temporarily to 1GB, and enable worker count auto-throttling.
riskLevel: CRITICAL - High Outage Risk for Ingress Gateway
impact: 100% of public traffic routed through srv-nginx-prod is failing with connection refused.
previousSimilarIncident: alt-22 (Ingress OOM on 2026-05-18, resolved by memory bump to 768MB)
commands: docker restart nginx-ingress; docker update --memory 1g nginx-ingress;

timeline.event: Search indexing crawler starts hammering /search route
Memory utilization on nginx-ingress hits 99.8% (511.2 MB)
OOM killer terminates nginx-ingress process (exit code 137)
Critical system down alert triggered by ping checks

comments.text: This is high priority. Steve, please approve the automatic remediation to restart and bump limits immediately.

title: SSL Certificate Expiring Soon
rootCause: Let's Encrypt automated cron job failed to renew because DNS verification failed.
aiAnalysis: SSL certificate for 'aime.internal.domain' expires in 14 days. The ACME renewal challenge failed due to a misconfigured TXT record on Route 53.
recommendedAction: Trigger manual DNS validation challenge or select Approve Action to provision a fallback certificate via AWS Certificate Manager.
impact: Browsers will display insecure warnings to all external clients if not renewed in 14 days.
commands: certbot renew --dns-route53; aws acm request-certificate --domain-name aime.internal.domain;

timeline.event: Daily automated ACME challenge triggered
TXT record check on Route 53 times out
ACME challenge failed. System warns SRE team of 14-day expiry window.

title: High CPU Usage on Web Load Balancer
rootCause: Spike in ingress web traffic (TCP handshake attempts up 350%).
aiAnalysis: Average CPU usage exceeded 85% for 15 minutes. Heavy cryptographic load for SSL handshakes is congesting core threads.
recommendedAction: Spin up an auto-scaled replica server in us-east-1b.
impact: Web frontend response latency has ticked up from 18ms to 65ms under high concurrency.
previousSimilarIncident: alt-08 (Traffic Spike on 2026-06-30, resolved by auto-scaling replica)

timeline.event: Concurrently active sockets increase from 1,200 to 4,500
CPU Core 0/1 core utilization sustains at 94.2%
Alert generated. Acknowledged by SRE Lead.

title: Kubernetes Pod CrashLoopBackOff
rootCause: Elasticsearch connection handshake timed out, throwing unhandled connection exception.
aiAnalysis: Liveness probe failed for Kibana replica. The Kibana application container cannot ping the central logging indices on port 9200, leading to process exit and subsequent CrashLoopBackOff restarts.
recommendedAction: Acknowledge Alert or approve container restart with delayed liveness probe checking (initialDelaySeconds: 60).
impact: Operators cannot view structured logs inside Kibana interface during the crash window.
commands: kubectl rollout restart deployment kibana-dashboard -n production-core;

timeline.event: Elasticsearch service restarts due to snapshot cleanups
Kibana connection pool throws Fatal Handshake Timeout
Pod crashes; liveness probes fail thrice consecutively
Rollout restart approved by SRE. Deployment fully healed.

comments.text: Healed. Increased initialDelaySeconds to 60 to give Elasticsearch plenty of time to accept socket registrations on startup.
